newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Select blue chips lead Hong Kong stocks rally.
newsitem.headline: Select blue chips lead Hong Kong stocks rally.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index hit a new high on Wednesday, but the surge in prices was led by a handful of the territory's blue chips in the property and banking sector, with other stocks lagging behind, analysts said.
"For the last 1,400 points on the index we really have not seen any meaningful amount of dispersion of buying," said Franklin Lam, director of research at HG Asia.

"Basically it's the top seven or eight in terms of market capitalisation that kept on setting all-time highs and they are principally the largest property stocks and also Hongkong Bank and Hang Seng Bank," he said.

The Hang Seng index jumped to a intra-day all-time high of 12,602.34 on Wednesday, carried by new records in shares of HSBC Holdings Plc (Hongkong Bank), Hang Seng Bank Ltd, Henderson Land Development Co Ltd and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd The previous intra-day record high was 12,599.23 points set on January 4, 1994.
The index later closed 94.52 points lower at 12,396.18 as investors took profits.
Hang Seng index constituents account for about 75 percent of total stock market capitalisation in Hong Kong, and property and banking stocks make up about 58 percent of the blue chip index.
Analysts said solid earnings growth from the property and banking sectors have prompted analysts to ramp up earnings estimates and encourage investors to remain invested.

"Although it may be towards the top end of traditional trading ranges, partly that is justified by earnings upgrades which I think are probably reasonable," said David Semple, equity strategist at Peregrine Research Institute.
Marshall Mays, chief strategist at Nikko Securities, said the situation was "quite volatile".
"It's money that is sort of hot actually. So it wants very large liquid shares, so it goes for the Cheung Kong, Henderson Land, the large caps," he said.
Some analysts said the chances were slim that other stocks would take over the charge.
"Most people are happily overweight and they don't feel the need to change their stock selection. Although we can come up with switching ideas, it is hard to make people sell," said Semple.
While the Hang Seng properties sub-index and the Hang Seng finance sub-index hit all-time highs on Wednesday, the utilities sub-index still has some way to go before reaching a record.

The Hang Seng utilities sub-index accounts for about 15 percent of the Hang Seng index capitalisation and achieved an all-time high on January 4, 1994 at 13,898.93. The index closed at 10,356.03 on Wednesday.

"Utilities really have not benefited too much on this rally," said Lam. "Normally people shift away from higher beta stocks -- lock in gains and put them into utilities and so on but we have not even seen that shift to safety."
He said the market was likely to meet resistance at current levels. "People are not quite willing to chase prices today."

Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, agreed. "I would say that the banks' outlook is pretty mixed from here. I think HSBC still has space to move but other banks are looking expensive."
"I'm not that optimistic on the market at this particular point," he added. "There is quite a lot of resistance around this 12,500 to 12,600 level."
